newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures remained hemmed into a narrow range on Tuesday with traders preoccupied by a series of potentially market moving events later in the week, including German and U.S. jobs reports.
Traders said there was some spread trading early in the session between French bonds and Bunds, with rumours of a weak German unemployment number due on Thursday again boosting the German market.
However, most said the March bond contract would be unlikely to make much progress ahead of the release of the key jobs reports on Thursday and Friday.

"Its been coin tossing sort of day I'm afraid," a trader at a French bank said. He said the U.S. jobs report due on Friday was probably less important than the German report at the moment given the resistance of European bonds to U.S. declines.
A futures trader at a U.S. house said he did not think the lows for the day at 132.06/08 constituted a very strong support and that a return to 131.50/60 was still on the cards.

A third trader at a French brokerage said the early boost to the market was driven by short covering after the rise in U.S. bonds overnight and he did not see the contract breaking out of a range between 131.86 and 132.30 before the jobs reports.
PIBOR contracts saw a slightly more active day, but traders said much of the business was driven by investors rolling March contracts over into June contracts ahead of the expiry on March 17.
Both March and June ended up two basis points, the return of the franc to close to 3.37 per mark providing a favourable backdrop for interest rate futures.

Analysts said investors remained nervous about potential market reactions to talk of a delay in European monetary union, despite the plethora of politicians and central bankers wheeled out during the past few days to try and calm the mood.
French markets, however, escaped any fallout. "There was really no interest for the French markets," a trader said.
Traders also said there was little activity in the cash market on Tuesday although there were some concerns about how successful Thursday's OAT auction would be.

The Treasury said on Tuesday it would be selling a total of 23 to 25 billion francs of OATs on March 6, of which a new January 25, 2009 TEC 10 OAT will make up eight to 10 billion francs. The other bond on sale will be the 5.50 percent benchmark 2007 OAT.

The franc was trading at 3.3724 per mark at 1615 GMT, up from 3.3750 late on Monday and yesterday's low of 3.3788. Against the dollar the franc fell to its lowest level this year touching 5.7847, down 11.5 percent so far in 1997.
